questions.question: What is an elastic material? Explain how an elastic band can store energy.
questions.expected_answer: An elastic material can be stretched, twisted or squashed and springs back to its shape when let go, like rubber. When we stretch or twist an elastic band, our muscles use energy, and some of it is stored in the band as long as it stays stretched or twisted.

questions.question: What is a spring, and how does it store energy? Give three everyday objects that contain springs.
questions.expected_answer: A spring is usually a coil of elastic steel wire. It stores energy when it is compressed or stretched. Examples: clicky pens, clothes pegs, staplers, mattresses, car suspension, trampolines, jack-in-the-box toys and wind-up clocks.

questions.question: Describe the elastic band investigation and what it showed.
questions.expected_answer: An elastic band was hooked on a ruler and stretched to 5, 10 and 15 cm, then released, and the distance it flew was measured. Only the stretch was changed, to keep it fair. The further it was stretched, the further it flew, showing that more stretch stores more energy.
